messages.author: e005eace5545a250
messages.subject: rma background correction problem
parts:
Hi,

We are trying to process 33 affy .cel files (custom PfSanger) and have
just installed aroma.affymetrix using R version 2.5.1 in Windows. Upon
creating the appropriate folders & directories etc we were unable to
successfully perform the background correction. We used the following
commands:

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("PFSANGERb520296")
> print(cdf)
AffymetrixCdfFile:
Path: annotationData/chipTypes/PFSANGERb520296
Filename: PFSANGERb520296.cdf
Filesize: 955.09MB
File format: v3 (text; ASCII)
Chip type: PFSANGERb520296
Dimension: 1600x1600
Number of cells: 2560000
Number of units: 2439101
Cells per unit: 1.05
Number of QC units: 9
RAM: 0.00MB
> path <- file.path("rawData", "PFDNAarrays_sept2007", "PFSANGERb520296")
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles(path)
> print(cs)
AffymetrixCelSet:
Name: PFDNAarrays_sept2007
Tags:
Path: rawData/PFDNAarrays_sept2007/PFSANGERb520296
Chip type: PFSANGERb520296
Number of arrays: 33
Names: Cathy10, Cathy11, ..., NF54-Inew
Time period: 2005-04-12 07:23:37 -- 2007-03-14 16:39:15
Total file size: 812.90MB
RAM: 0.02MB
> bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
> verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
> timestampOn(verbose)

and encountered the following errors:

Windows:
"Microsoft visual C++ runtime library error. This application has
requested the runtime to terminate it in an unusual way. Please
contact the applications support team for more information"

and upon closing the R gui:
"The instruction at "0x5ad71531" referenced memory at "0x00000014".
The memory could not be 'read'

Is there an obvious reason why we were unable to successfully
background correct?
(NB. We were able to previously successfully perform the background
correction using RMAExpress)

We then performed the quantile normalization successfully and are
currently fitting the probe linear model
i.e.
> plm <- RmaCnPlm(csN, combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE)
> print(plm)
> fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

however, this is taking some time (estimated time to completion
2.8days...). Is this simply due to the large number of probe sets (ca.
2.5 million)?

Cheers,
Alex & Celine

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] rma background correction problem
parts:
Hi.

First of all, it is much faster (and much more memory efficient) to
work with binary CDF files rather than ASCII ones, cf. FAQ
(2007-07-09) on the group page. See same FAQ for instructions how to
convert. [In a future version, the package might through an error by
default whenever one tries to use an ASCII version.]

I am not sure why RmaBackgroundCorrection would cause R to crash.
Please report sessionInfo() and traceback(), and relevant output from
using verbose output (when calling process()). However, from previous
experience I would suspect this is related to the CDF file, cf. FAQ
(2007-07-13). Simply retry with the binary CDF and let us know if it
help (repost). [ A wild guess could be that you are running out of
memory when you try to read from the ASCII CDF which is already 955MB.
When affxparser/FusionSDK read even a subset of an ASCII CDF, it is
to the best of my understanding that it actually has to read all of
the CDF first, then extract the subset of interest. On Windows you've
typically only have 2GB/3GB RAM. ]

That you experience summarization to be slow, could, in addition to be
due to an ASCII CDF file, also be (quoting a previous reply) "related
to what Ken noticed for the human exon array where for instance one
unit has ~17000 probes(!), cf.

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram

The fitting time grows exponentially(?) with the number of
probes/chips. Thus, for such large units alternative
modeling/algorithms have to be found. I do not know of any work that
attacks this problem.". Basically, if you only have a few units with
a large number of cells, see if you can avoid fitting those. See the
above URL for how to identify large units. Let us know if this could
be case and/or if you see a speed up (repost).

For future correspondence, please try to separate different issues in
different message.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.author: 41ed89aa70b5d27c
messages.subject: Re: rma background correction problem
parts:
On Sep 6, 2:47 am, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> I am not sure why RmaBackgroundCorrection would cause R to crash.
> Please report sessionInfo() and traceback(), and relevant output from
> using verbose output (when calling process()). However, from previous
> experience I would suspect this is related to the CDF file, cf. FAQ
> (2007-07-13). Simply retry with the binary CDF and let us know if it
> help (repost). [ A wild guess could be that you are running out of
> memory when you try to read from the ASCII CDF which is already 955MB.
> When affxparser/FusionSDK read even a subset of an ASCII CDF, it is
> to the best of my understanding that it actually has to read all of
> the CDF first, then extract the subset of interest. On Windows you've
> typically only have 2GB/3GB RAM. ]

This is not correct. Affxparser uses memory mapping which (as far as I
understands) _allocates_ memory for the entire CDF file. But I am
pretty sure that the entries in the CDF files are not moved into
memory from disk until a function needs them. Of course that _may_ be
prompted by doing such a thing as requesting all unit names (whether
that just parses the unit names or the entire unit is not known to
me).

This is at least the explanation I got quite some time ago from one of
the lead Fusion developers. Of course details may vary regarding to
file version etc.

Kasper

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: rma background correction problem
parts:
Hi.

Yes, it looks like the previous problem with R crashing went away when
you converted to a binary CDF. The problem you've reported below is
unrelated to the RmaBackgroundCorrection class. I think you get the
same error if you just do:
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("PFSANGERb520296")

cells <- getCellIndices(cdf, verbose=-20)

Correct? However, I still believe you're running into memory issues
on Windows, that is, that you are using up all available memory that a
single R process can allocate (which is typically 2GB RAM or 3GB if
you really know the tricks). The reason why I believe so is because I
see the output "Failed to read the CDF file.", and I remember I've
seen myself on Windows when I was really pushing the memory limits; at
some stage affxparser/FusionSDK failed to read my CDF which normally
worked fine. Your CDF got 2,439,101 units, which is the biggest
number I've seen this far (I've done 1.8*10^6 units myself on
Windows). BTW, is this a tiling array? FYI, I don't know of anyone
that used aroma.affymetrix for tiling arrays, but someone has to be
the first, ehe ;)

Is there anyway you can make the CDF file available to me so I can try
it out on my Windows machine? Is it downloadable from somewhere? If
you make it available to me, could you please make sure to zip/gzip it
first (that would bring it down to ~200-250MB). You may forward me
the URL offline if you wish too.

Cheers

Henrik

Hi Henrik.

It is indeed a memory issue. We were unable to make the binary CDF
on Windows, so we tried it on unix23 (our powerful unix machine) and
it worked.

We are actually able to run:

x<-getCellIndices(cdf)

successfully when going back to R (from a clean session) on Windows.

The commands below that failed on Windows worked ok on unix (on a
small number of chips), but consumed ~4Gb of RAM in the process ...
mostly at the "Obtaining signals..." stage where the getCellIndices
is called. We are going to continue with processing the data on unix
and see how far we can get.

The CDF file is 428Mb binary, unzipped. We'll see how we go and if
all else fails, we'll pass it on to you.

Cheers,
Mark

> it worked.
>

>
> x<-getCellIndices(cdf)
>
> successfully when going back to R (from a clean session) on Windows.

Ok, this is what I suspected too. It might also be that it will work
better on R v2.6.x, because there's been some memory optimization in
how strings are stored (support for suffix trees added). That might
bring you down to below the Windows limit.

>
> The commands below that failed on Windows worked ok on unix (on a
> small number of chips), but consumed ~4Gb of RAM in the process ...
> mostly at the "Obtaining signals..." stage where the getCellIndices
> is called. We are going to continue with processing the data on unix
> and see how far we can get.

It is possible to update aroma.affymetrix and/or affxparser to deal
with the problem (e.g. unlist(getCellIndices(cdf), use.names=FALSE)
can be done in chunks etc), but if you can run it on Unix, that's
better.

Cheers

Henrik

FYI, as you might have already seen, aroma.affymetrix v0.6.2 does now
use much less memory when it extracts the cell indices for the
RmaBackgroundCorrection, e.g. instead of using 1400MB for
GenomeWideSNP_6 it now uses only 60MB. So, I think you should be able
to process the PFSANGERb520296 chip type on Windows now.

Cheers

Henrik
